project.name: Music Wizard :: Integration Tests
project.description:
Tests that span modules. Mostly the slow, externally-dependent ones -- model downloads, LilyPond invocation, the MIDI to audio to Score ground-truth loop -- which are named *IT and only run under -Pintegration.
Three are neither slow nor externally dependent and are named *Test, so surefire runs them in the default build. MidiRoundTripTest exports a Score through mw-notation and reads it back through mw-transcribe, and StaffNotationOverloadTest reads what the emitter writes for a played passage; both need audio, model and binary alike not at all, and both are here because neither module may depend on the other -- mw-notation must not see the audio and DSP stack mw-transcribe is built on, and mw-transcribe has no business emitting notation -- and this is the module that already depends on both. (Until #247, the sharper version of that was "mw-transcribe pulls in mw-ml, which the notation layer is not allowed to see"; the edge is gone but the rule it illustrated is not.) LilyPondComplaintsTest reads LilyPond's diagnostics without running it, and explains there why it belongs here.
The rule, from #148 and #155: a test that needs no LilyPond is named *Test, whatever else is in the file it was written in. What that buys is which job runs it -- every `mvn verify` and every CI job, rather than only the one where someone remembered -Pintegration, which is the job #145 showed can stay red and unread for weeks. It does not buy noticing a test that stops running: failIfNoTests is not configured here, so a *Test that disappears is as silent as an *IT that does.
`mvn verify` stays fast, offline and binary-free either way.
